newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-JUVE AND UNITED TAKE GIANT STEPS IN TITLE DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVE AND UNITED TAKE GIANT STEPS IN TITLE DEFENCE.

text.p: Juventus and Manchester United took giant steps towards retaining their league titles by winning while key rivals lost. Barcelona crashed 4-0 to boost Real Madrid's championship bid in Spain, PSG and Auxerre crashed out of the French Cup while the leading pair in Germany both notched up handsome victories.
Following is a summary of the action from the top European leagues this weekend:
Italy

Juventus, who look likely to celebrate their 100th anniversary year with a record 24th league title, tightened their grip on the championship with a 2-0 victory over Italian Cup finalists Vicenza on Saturday.
Italy midfielder Angelo Di Livio scored his first serie A goal of the season for Juve. Michele Padovano scored their second from the penalty spot.
Parma, Inter and Sampdoria are locked in what now looks like a race to finish second in Serie A.

Sampdoria slipped up 2-1 at home to Bologna for whom Russian Igor Kolyvanov scored twice, including a dramatic last-minute winner. Inter won 3-0 at Piacenza in another Saturday fixture, and Parma beat relegation-threatened Cagliari 3-2 thanks largely to a pair of goals from Argentine Hernan Crespo.
England
Manchester United enjoyed one of their best weekends of the season, beating Coventry 3-1 while title rivals Newcastle, Liverpool, Chelsea and Wimbledon all lost.
United's win came courtesy of two Coventry own goals in the first five minutes of Saturday's match. Czech Karel Poborsky added the champions' third.

Newcastle slipped up 1-0 at home to relegation-threatened Southampton, for whom England midfielder Matt LeTissier scored a vital winner. Liverpool lost 1-0 at fifth-placed Aston Villa in Sunday's match and are now four points adrift of the leaders.
Third-placed Arsenal won 2-0 at Everton.
Spain

Barcelona's beleaguered coach Bobby Robson saw two of his players sent off in his side's 4-0 league defeat at Tenerife. The former England manager refused to discuss his position at the club in a post-match press conference.
Leaders Real Madrid will go nine points clear of their arch-rivals if they win at Espanyol in Monday's match.

Barcelona now also have Deportivo Coruna, Atletico Madrid and Real Betis breathing down their necks. All three sides won at the weekend to throw the race for Spain's second champions' league place wide open. Betis can go level with Barcelona if they win on Thursday at Sporting Gijon in a game postponed from January.
France
Paris St Germain crashed out of the French Cup 4-3 on penalties to Clermont after the fourth division side had recovered from 4-1 to draw 4-4 in normal time of their third round tie on Saturday.
Goalkeeper Olivier Enjoiras, a clothes salesman, put the amateurs into the quarter-finals by saving the penalties of defender Paul Le Guen and midfielder Vincent Guerin.
It was the second major upset of an extraordinary cup competition in 24 hours, following Auxerre's stunning loss to second division Troyes on Friday.
Only four of the quarter-finalists are top flight sides and only one, Bordeaux, is from the top ten in the first division.
Germany
Italy-bound Christian Ziege struck twice as Bayern Munich stayed three points clear with a 5-2 thrashing of unglamorous Duisburg on Saturday.
The Bavarians could even afford the luxury of missing a second-half penalty after first-half goals from Juergen Klinsmann and Mario Basler and an own goal from Markus Reiter.
Champions Borussia Dortmund were also in goalscoring mood, winning 4-1 at home over middle-of-the-table 1860 Munich to stay second.
Bayer Leverkusen, who started the day level on points with Dortmund, lost ground in the race thanks to a goalless draw at lowly Fortuna Duesseldorf.
Portugal
Leaders and defending champions Porto could only draw 2-2 at Amadora in Friday's match. Second-placed Sporting took advantage by beating Leca 1-0 but Lisbon's other giants Benfica lost 3-1 at Chaves.
Netherlands
PSV Eindhoven maintaned their three-point lead over Feyenoord by beating RKC Waalwijk 4-1 away on Sunday.
On Saturday Argentine striker Pablo Sanchez scored both goals as Feyenoord beat bottom club NEC Nijmegen 2-0.
Champions Ajax Amsterdam, whose away match against Sparta Rotterdam was postponed because of fears of crowd trouble, remain fifth.
